column1: If CðpÞ > GðpÞ, the central bank will not have an incentive to cheat, and inflation at the rate p can be supported. But suppose the central bank does cheat. Will it be in the interests of a private sector that has somehow coordinated on a trigger strategy to actually punish the central bank? If by punishing the central bank the private sector also punishes itself, the threat to punish may not be credible. If punishment is not credible, the central bank is not deterred from cheating in the first place.
